title: Sell Mineral Rights in Millsboro, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Millsboro, PA | Washington County
metaDescription: Millsboro, PA sits along the Monongahela in Washington County. We buy mineral and royalty interests directly, with a clear-eyed look at your deed history.
heroLead: Millsboro sits along the Monongahela River in Washington County, a small river community where mining history and modern Marcellus leasing sit layered on top of each other.
intro: Like a lot of towns along the Mon River corridor, Millsboro's ground carries a mining past that shaped how mineral rights got divided long before anyone thought about shale gas. Coal companies severed rights here decades ago, and untangling exactly what your family retained takes real title work, not guesswork.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Millsboro directly. We do that research through the county records ourselves and explain what we find before ever discussing a number with you.

sections.heading: River Towns and Severed Estates
paragraphs: Mining operations along the Monongahela near Millsboro often purchased coal rights outright while leaving oil and gas with the original landowner, which is a favorable situation if that's how your family's history worked out. Other tracts saw broader mineral reservations that covered oil and gas along with coal, which is a different situation entirely.
We can't tell which applies to your parcel without checking the actual recorded documents, so that's always our starting point rather than an assumption either way.

sections.heading: Marcellus Activity Around Millsboro
paragraphs: Washington County remains one of the most heavily leased and drilled counties in the Marcellus wet-gas window, and operators have continued developing acreage throughout the townships surrounding Millsboro. If your interest is tied to an active unit, recent royalty history will tell us far more than the well's original completion report.
We ask for whatever statements you have and walk through them with you so the deductions and allocated production actually make sense before we talk value.

sections.heading: Confirming Your Chain of Title
paragraphs: We research your deed history through the Washington County Recorder of Deeds, checking for any coal severance language that might affect how your oil and gas interest reads today.

faqs.question: How do I know if coal rights were severed separately from my gas rights?
faqs.answer: It requires checking your recorded deed history for reservation language. We do that research as part of our review, at no cost to you, before making an offer.

faqs.question: Is my interest along the river worth less because of the mining history?
faqs.answer: Not inherently. Mining history affects title complexity, not the underlying value of your oil and gas rights, which we evaluate separately.

faqs.question: What's the fastest way to get an accurate read on my interest?
faqs.answer: Send us your deed and any lease or royalty paperwork you have. That's usually enough for us to start the title and production review.
